players.product: temporary bonders / debonders for HBM wafer thinning, UV projection scanners and coaters for CoWoS, die-to-wafer hybrid bonders

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Cornelia Ballwießer: H1 2026 sales were EUR 202.8 million, as expected and EUR 63.8 million below the record H1 2025 (CEO Burkhardt Frick); gross margin was 37.2%, including a one-time EUR 2.1 million charge for a withdrawn Advanced Backend Solutions product, and the EBIT margin rose to 9% in Q2 from 4.3% in Q1 as Q1 marked the low point. Advanced Backend Solutions turned around with a 12.1% Q2 EBIT margin (H1 EBIT EUR 8.3 million, 5.6% margin), helped by bonding sales; Photomask Solutions had a 39.5% Q2 gross margin (43% in Q1) and a 12.4% EBIT margin, with sales below prior year after weak 2025 order intake. H1 free cash flow was EUR 16.4 million and cash EUR 112.3 million; contract liabilities rose EUR 33.8 million on customer advance payments, particularly for the stronger China business.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 sales EUR 202.8 million; Q2 EBIT margin 9%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Burkhardt Frick: H1 2026 order intake was EUR 410 million, already above full-year 2025, with Q2 at EUR 260 million, the highest quarterly order intake in SUSS's history; more than 40 coaters were booked in May and June alone, including a single EUR 115 million order for spin coaters from a Taiwanese advanced packaging customer that will significantly scale capacity and also serves the biggest foundry in Taiwan, where SUSS is the qualified tool of record. Excluding that order, intake was at about the EUR 140 million level per quarter, broad across bonding, photomask and imaging; most orders are tied to AI applications, with fewer bonder orders and many more OSAT-related packaging orders. The order book reached a record of about EUR 476 million at the end of H1 (EUR 473.7 million in the outlook), of which around EUR 240 million is expected to convert to sales in H2 2026 and approximately EUR 220 million is scheduled for delivery in 2027, which management says is not a 2027 guidance.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 order intake EUR 410 million; order book about EUR 476 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Burkhardt Frick: SUSS confirmed its 2026 guidance of sales of EUR 425 million-EUR 485 million, a 35%-37% gross margin and an 8%-10% EBIT margin, with a stronger second half; the window for orders converting into 2026 sales is closing, few production slots remain, and customers now give request dates far beyond SUSS's lead times, with big bookings all the way to the end of 2027, possibly due to industry shortages. He declined to forecast order intake, noting that customers may have pulled orders forward in anticipation of equipment or parts shortages.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 sales EUR 425 million-EUR 485 million; EBIT margin 8%-10%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Burkhardt Frick: the record spin-coater orders (200 and 300-millimeter) are being built in parallel at the Taiwan and German sites, and the new Taiwanese factory gives room to add space and manpower; 'getting parts is becoming also an issue', but SUSS can confirm the orders received. COO Thomas Rohe: SUSS expects no change in its lead times despite some problems rising in the supply chain from the huge demand; temporary bonders / debonders and scanners have a half-year minimum lead time and their 2026 slots are taken. CEO: SUSS partially intends to raise prices where it has solid grounds, mainly through new products.

CEO Burkhardt Frick: SUSS launched its first panel-level UV production scanner, now at a customer site in a pilot line where the customer will develop the CoPoS process; volume orders for newly introduced products are expected in 2027 and beyond. The mid-end cleaner, the second new product, launches and ships this year with POs in the high single digits and the first machines built in H2; the first wafer cleaner (200 millimeter) is validating in SUSS's application center with customer wafers and is to ship next year, with a 300 millimeter version starting development. Follow-up volume orders typically come after a six to 12 month qualification, with some in H1 2027 and more in H2 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: mid-end cleaner POs in the high single digits

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Burkhardt Frick: in temporary bonding for HBM SUSS has a strong share in the HBM3E mix, but sees no current momentum from one Korean customer, where competition is significant and process records are changing. A second Korean customer booked an order in early Q1, the system was delivered towards the end of Q2 and another is in the pipeline, SUSS's hardware being in after a long struggle; at the non-Korean customer SUSS is raising throughput and yield of its installed base until that customer's new site is ready, not before the beginning of next year, and will install additional machines in H2 where space allows. A third Korean customer's utilization is rising but has brought no substantial volume orders.

CFO Cornelia Ballwießer: Americas rose to 14.1% of H1 2026 order intake from 9.5% as the push for localized production in America and EMEA turns into tool orders; APAC was 75.5% (76.7% in 2025) and China fell to 22.4% from 30.2% while rising in absolute terms to EUR 69.4 million. APAC's share of sales fell to around 75% from 84% in a digestion phase after the initial ramp, with EMEA at 10% and Americas at 15%. CEO Burkhardt Frick: Chinese activity picked up in the last two quarters and that momentum can increase further.
quarterly_data.figure: China order intake EUR 69.4 million in H1 2026

quarterly_data.signal: COO Thomas Rohe: SUSS will build a new application and R&D center in Karlsruhe, close to the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, relocating parts of R&D and application work from Sternenfels; it is not about adding capacity, and subject to approvals the facility is expected to be completed in 2028.
